messages.content: Mark got Thursday and Friday approved, so San Antonio is now Thursday April 9 to Sunday April 12. Can you rerun the best flight and hotel combo for the three of us? I’m trying to decide between the pricier nonstop and the cheaper one-stop, and between the River Walk hotel with the pool versus the bigger breakfast-included place farther out.

Here is the clean comparison. Flights: Option A is ATL-SAT nonstop Thursday late morning, arriving around lunchtime, paired with the Sunday midafternoon nonstop back to Atlanta. It costs more, but it preserves most of Thursday and avoids connection risk. Option B is the cheaper one-stop outbound, but it arrives mid-to-late afternoon and uses up a lot of the first day. Return choices: the late-morning nonstop is a little cheaper but makes Sunday feel like packing and leaving; the midafternoon nonstop gives you breakfast and a short River Walk or Alamo window before the airport. Hotels: the River Walk option has the stronger location, pool, very good guest ratings, and easy dinner access, but breakfast is paid. The farther-out suite is roomier and includes breakfast, but you would spend more time and money on rideshares.
Can you put rough dollars around that? Especially once we add breakfast and rideshares.

Approximate all-in difference for the three nights: River Walk hotel is about $235 to $270 more than the farther-out suite before breakfast. If you stay farther out and rely on rideshares, I would budget $140 to $200 for airport, dinners, River Walk, and Alamo trips, depending on how often you come back midday. Breakfast at the River Walk hotel could run $45 to $65 for the three of you if you use the hotel restaurant, but nearby casual breakfast can keep that lower. Net: the farther-out hotel is still cheaper, but not by the headline hotel-rate difference.
The one-stop savings are tempting. Are we giving up too much of Thursday?

I think yes. The one-stop saves roughly $80 to $95 per person, but it turns Thursday into a travel-heavy day and gives you a connection with a child during spring-break travel. For a three-night trip, the nonstop is the better value if the budget can absorb it.
And Sunday? I don’t want to drag everyone to the airport at breakfast time.

Then take the midafternoon return. The late-morning return would likely mean leaving the hotel around 8:45 or 9:00 after packing. The midafternoon nonstop lets you do a relaxed breakfast, maybe a short Alamo visit or River Walk stroll, then head to SAT around 12:30.
Is the pool enough reason to take the River Walk hotel even with paid breakfast?

For this trip, I would count the pool plus location together, not the pool alone. The River Walk hotel gives you easier evenings, less transit planning, and a built-in kid break if the weather cooperates. Paid breakfast is annoying, but easier to work around than being farther out every night.
Any reason to check Austin again?

Not unless Austin is dramatically cheaper. Once you add the drive, rental or transfer cost, and the time lost on both ends, it would need to save several hundred dollars total to beat flying into SAT for a short family weekend.
Can we hold this, or do we need to book tonight?

The hotel should be booked as refundable if you want flexibility. The airfare is the less stable piece; if the fare class changes, the nonstop combo could jump. If your booking portal offers a 24-hour cancellation window after ticketing, I would book tonight rather than leave it in a cart.
So final pick is the Thursday nonstop, Sunday midafternoon nonstop, and River Walk refundable room?

Yes. My recommendation is: book the simple ATL-SAT nonstop Thursday, the Sunday midafternoon SAT-ATL nonstop, and the refundable two-queen River Walk hotel. I would skip the one-stop and skip Austin. Before payment, verify the hotel cancellation deadline, whether breakfast is truly paid and not bundled, pool hours, and that the room type is two queens for all three of you.

messages.content: Let’s finalize San Antonio. The Thursday outbound and Sunday 2:45-ish nonstop are still available, but the fare is up a little. The River Walk refundable two-queen room is also still showing. Can you walk me through the last choices before I click?

Yes. Final package to verify: three travelers, ATL to SAT nonstop Thursday Apr 9, arriving before early afternoon; SAT to ATL nonstop Sunday Apr 12 around 2:45 p.m.; refundable River Walk hotel, two queens, pool, walkable restaurants, breakfast not included. I would avoid basic economy if it removes seat selection or makes changes harder.
Use the saved traveler profiles for me, Mark, and Nia. The names and TSA PreCheck numbers are current for the adults. What are the seat choices?

No-fee seats together are available as 20A/20B/20C outbound and 24A/24B/24C return. There is also a closer return row, 15A/15B/15C, but it is showing a fee for each seat. I would keep the no-fee sets together unless being closer to the front is worth paying extra.
Put Nia by the window outbound. For the return I’ll take the window unless she insists. Main thing is not splitting us up.

Good. Outbound: Nia 20A, you 20B, Mark 20C. Return: you 24A, Nia 24B, Mark 24C, and you can swap onboard if she wants the window. That keeps all three together and avoids paying for a small row improvement.
What about fare type? I don’t want to accidentally lose the seat assignments.
Choose main cabin or the equivalent standard economy fare, not basic. The small savings on basic are not worth the risk of losing advance seat control or flexibility with a family itinerary.
Hotel requests: away from elevator noise, and not a low floor if possible. Should I add early check-in?

Yes, add it as a request, not an assumption. Suggested note: arriving early afternoon; would appreciate early check-in if available; if not, luggage storage requested. Also add: quiet room away from elevator and ice machine, higher floor preferred, two queen beds confirmed.
Should I prepay the hotel breakfast?

I would not prepay unless the bundle is clearly discounted and cancellable. Since you will be on the River Walk, keep breakfast flexible: hotel restaurant on a rainy or slow morning, nearby casual places on other days.
Okay, book the flights and the refundable River Walk room with those seats and requests.

Ready to submit with main cabin flights, no-fee family seating, refundable two-queen River Walk room, and the quiet-room plus early-arrival notes. Please confirm you want to proceed with the slightly higher fare and the saved payment method.
Confirmed. Use the saved card ending 4421.

Booked. Plan is set for Thu Apr 9-Sun Apr 12: ATL-SAT nonstop outbound, SAT-ATL midafternoon nonstop return, seats 20A/B/C outbound and 24A/B/C return, refundable two-queen River Walk hotel, breakfast not included, pool on site, and requests added for quiet room, higher floor, early check-in if available, and luggage storage if the room is not ready. Next checks: cancellation deadline, pool hours, seat map at check-in, and weather for first-night dinner.

messages.content: Can you give me a compact checklist for Thursday? Flights and hotel are booked, but the forecast looks warm and stormy, pool hours are limited Friday, and the room may not be ready when we arrive.

Thursday checklist: leave Decatur with a spring-break buffer; get to ATL early enough for one checked bag and a kid-paced security line; keep IDs, snacks, chargers, swimsuits, and one light rain layer accessible. At SAT, use rideshare to the River Walk hotel, drop bags if the room is not ready, and ask again about pool hours. For the first evening, pick an indoor or covered dinner plan. Friday: Alamo or River Walk earlier in the day, pool only if hours/weather line up, and keep a museum or indoor activity as backup.
How early would you actually get to ATL for the 10:25 departure if we check one bag?
I would aim to be inside the terminal around 8:15 to 8:30. That gives room for bag drop, family bathroom stops, and spring-break security without making the morning painfully early.
If the room is not ready, what should we do between luggage drop and dinner if storms hit?

Drop luggage, keep a small day bag with rain jackets and any meds, then choose lunch or a snack somewhere indoor near the River Walk. If storms are active, avoid planning the boat ride that afternoon; save it for Friday or Saturday and use the hotel lobby, nearby shops, or a short indoor museum stop as the buffer.
Breakfast alternatives near the hotel? I don’t want to be locked into the hotel buffet.

Check hours for La Panadería, Schilo’s, and any hotel-adjacent coffee spots before you leave. For Sunday, choose somewhere quick or close so you are not rushing before the 12:30-ish airport departure.
Seat map changed: I see 18A/B/C outbound for $21 each and 21A/B/C return for free. Worth moving?

Move the return to 21A/B/C since it is free and closer than 24A/B/C. I would skip paying $63 total just to move from row 20 to row 18 outbound. Keep the family together, recheck again at online check-in, and only pay if a meaningfully better adjacent row opens.
